name: PriorityClass & preemption
objective: CKA › Workloads & Scheduling. A PriorityClass stamps pods with a priority value; the scheduler places higher-priority pods first and, on a full node, will PREEMPT (evict) lower-priority pods to make room. Create PriorityClasses and use them, then watch a high-priority pod preempt low-priority ballast on a full node.

questions.title: Create PriorityClasses and use one
questions.teach:
A **PriorityClass** is a cluster-scoped object mapping a name to an integer `value` (higher = more important). A pod opts in with `priorityClassName`; the admission controller copies the number into the pod's `.spec.priority`. The scheduler orders the pending queue by priority and uses it to decide preemption.

**Gotcha:** `globalDefault: true` applies a PriorityClass to pods that don't name one (only one default allowed). Values above 1,000,000,000 are reserved for system-critical classes.
questions.prompt:
Create two PriorityClasses: `high-priority` (value `1000000`) and `low-priority` (value `100`). Then in namespace `priority-learn` run pod `important` (image `nginx:1.25`) with `priorityClassName: high-priority`.

Target: PriorityClass `high-priority` has value 1000000; pod `important` uses it and its `.spec.priority` is `1000000`.
questions.hint: `kubectl create priorityclass high-priority --value=1000000` and `--value=100` for low-priority. Then a pod with `spec.priorityClassName: high-priority`. Check: `kubectl -n priority-learn get pod important -o jsonpath='{.spec.priority}'`.
questions.solution:
kubectl create priorityclass high-priority --value=1000000 2>/dev/null
kubectl create priorityclass low-priority --value=100 2>/dev/null
kubectl create namespace priority-learn 2>/dev/null
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: important, namespace: priority-learn }
spec:
  priorityClassName: high-priority
  containers:
  - name: web
    image: nginx:1.25
YAML

verification.description: PriorityClass high-priority=1000000 and pod important uses it (.spec.priority=1000000)

questions.title: Preemption: evict low-priority to fit high
questions.teach:
When a higher-priority pod can't schedule because a node is full, the scheduler **preempts** — it evicts one or more lower-priority pods on a node to make room, then places the high-priority pod. Preempted pods are deleted (and recreated by their controller, where they may sit Pending).

**Gotcha:** preemption only fires when there's genuinely no room — the scheduler picks the fewest/lowest-priority victims. A pod can opt out of causing preemption with `preemptionPolicy: Never` (it still schedules by priority, just never evicts others).
questions.prompt:
Setup pinned two low-priority `ballast` pods (PriorityClass `demo-low`) onto `$W1`, filling it. Create a high-priority pod `vip` in `priority-learn` (image `nginx:1.25`, `priorityClassName: demo-high`, `nodeSelector prio-demo=yes`, CPU request `1000m`) — the scheduler must preempt a ballast pod to place it.

Target: `vip` is `Running` on `$W1`, and the scheduler preempted at least one `ballast` pod (fewer remain running).
questions.hint: Create `vip` with `priorityClassName: demo-high`, `nodeSelector: {prio-demo: yes}`, and `resources.requests.cpu: 1000m`. The node is full of demo-low ballast, so the scheduler evicts one to fit vip. Watch: `kubectl -n priority-learn get pods -w`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: { name: vip, namespace: priority-learn, labels: { role: vip } }
spec:
  priorityClassName: demo-high
  nodeSelector: { prio-demo: "yes" }
  containers:
  - name: web
    image: nginx:1.25
    resources: { requests: { cpu: 1000m } }
YAML
kubectl -n priority-learn get pods -o wide -w

verification.description: vip Running on $W1 after preempting a low-priority ballast pod
